questionText:
Consider a sequence $a$ of elements $a_0 = 1, a_1 = 5, a_2 = 7, a_3 = 8, a_4 = 9$, and $a_5 = 2$. The following operations are performed on a stack $S$ and a queue $Q$, both of which are initially empty.

I: $\text{push}$ the elements of $a$ from $a_0$ to $a_5$ in that order into $S$.
II: $\text{enqueue}$ the elements of $a$ from $a_0$ to $a_5$ in that order into $Q$.
III: $\text{pop}$ an element from $S$.
IV: $\text{dequeue}$ an element from $Q$.
V: $\text{pop}$ an element from $S$.
VI: $\text{dequeue}$ an element from $Q$.
VII: $\text{dequeue}$ an element from $Q$ and $\text{push}$ the same element into $S$.
VIII: Repeat operation VII three times.
IX: $\text{pop}$ an element from $S$.
X: $\text{pop}$ an element from $S$.

The $\text{top}$ element of $S$ after executing the above operations is ____________.
explanation:
Let us trace the operations step-by-step:

Initial State:
Sequence $a = [1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 2]$
Stack $S = []$
Queue $Q = []$

I: Push elements $a_0$ through $a_5$ into $S$:
$S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 2]$ (top = $2$)

II: Enqueue elements $a_0$ through $a_5$ into $Q$:
$Q = [1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 2]$ (front = $1$)

III: Pop from $S$:
Pops $2 \rightarrow S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 9]$

IV: Dequeue from $Q$:
Dequeues $1 \rightarrow Q = [5, 7, 8, 9, 2]$

V: Pop from $S$:
Pops $9 \rightarrow S = [1, 5, 7, 8]$

VI: Dequeue from $Q$:
Dequeues $5 \rightarrow Q = [7, 8, 9, 2]$

VII: Dequeue from $Q$ and push to $S$:
Dequeues $7 \rightarrow Q = [8, 9, 2]$
Pushes $7 \rightarrow S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7]$

VIII: Repeat operation VII 3 times:
1. Dequeue 8, push 8: $Q = [9, 2], S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7, 8]$
2. Dequeue 9, push 9: $Q = [2], S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7, 8, 9]$
3. Dequeue 2, push 2: $Q = [], S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7, 8, 9, 2]$

IX: Pop from $S$:
Pops $2 \rightarrow S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7, 8, 9]$

X: Pop from $S$:
Pops $9 \rightarrow S = [1, 5, 7, 8, 7, 8]$

The top element of $S$ is 8.
